Drohobych Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Drohobych's Jewish community, documented from 1404, grew into a major presence in the city's oil industry — by the late 19th century, 80 percent of employees in Drohobych's oil refineries were Jewish. The brothers Maurycy (1856–1879), a realist painter of the Romantic period, and Leopold (1883–1934), a modernist painter, were both born in the city. A Hebrew-lettered, German-language newspaper, the Drohobitzer Zeitung, was published weekly in the early 20th century. This is the older of Drohobych's two Jewish cemeteries, presumed established in the 17th century and used until the end of the 19th century.
